hints: Resolve forces vertically on the ring in equilibrium: the normal reaction R and the upward component $8\sin 10^\circ$ balance the downward weight $mg = 0.3g$.
Use the kinetic friction formula $F = \mu R$ with $\mu = 0.8$ once R is calculated.
Apply Newton's second law horizontally: the forward component $8\cos 10^\circ$ minus friction F equals $ma$, where $m = 0.3\text{ kg}$, to determine acceleration a.
Use the SUVAT equation $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$ with $u = 0$ and $s = 0.6\text{ m}$ to find the time taken.
walkthrough:
Identify the four forces acting on the ring of mass $0.3\text{ kg}$:
- Pulling force $8\text{ N}$ at $10^\circ$ above the horizontal.
- Downward gravitational force: $W = mg = (0.3)(10) = 3\text{ N}$.
- Upward normal reaction force from the rod: $R$.
- Friction force $F$ directed backwards along the rod opposing motion.

Resolve forces vertically perpendicular to the rod. Since the ring does not accelerate vertically:
$$\sum F_y = 0$$
$$R + 8\sin 10^\circ - mg = 0$$
$$R = mg - 8\sin 10^\circ$$
Substitute $m = 0.3\text{ kg}$ and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$R = 0.3(10) - 8\sin 10^\circ = 3 - 8(0.173648) = 3 - 1.38918 = 1.61082\text{ N}$$

Calculate the friction force using $F = \mu R$ with coefficient $\mu = 0.8$:
$$F = 0.8(1.61082) = 1.28866\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law along the horizontal rod in the direction of motion:
$$\sum F_x = ma$$
$$8\cos 10^\circ - F = ma$$
Substitute the evaluated values and $m = 0.3\text{ kg}$:
$$8(0.984808) - 1.28866 = 0.3a$$
$$7.87846 - 1.28866 = 0.3a$$
$$6.58980 = 0.3a$$
Divide both sides by $0.3$:
$$a = \frac{6.58980}{0.3} \approx 21.9660\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Use the SUVAT displacement-time relation from rest ($u = 0$) over distance $s = 0.6\text{ m}$:
$$s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$$
$$0.6 = 0 + \frac{1}{2}(21.9660)t^2$$
$$0.6 = 10.9830 t^2$$
Divide by $10.9830$:
$$t^2 = \frac{0.6}{10.9830} \approx 0.054630$$
Take the square root:
$$t = \sqrt{0.054630} \approx 0.23373\text{ s}$$
Rounding to three significant figures gives:
$$t = 0.234\text{ s}$$
